messages:
oncall-bot: 🔔 Pager: gpu_vram_oom_rate firing on cluster-prod-west (gpu-wn-17). Severity: P2. Affected service: inference-hosting. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-453

sam: on it. paging and joining. first check: are any user-facing routes backed by this node?

maya: looks like a Dedicated pool node, running batch fallback and some long-lived customer sessions. CPU fine, VRAM trending up quickly. ECC errors also spiking on nvme-sensor logs.

sam: copying logs: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-wn-17` shows 7 pods, 3 are our low-priority batch-runner replicas.

devon: FYI routing: canary fallback has 2 spare nodes in same AZ, traffic should shift for new sessions. existing sessions pinned -> some customers may see degraded throughput.

sam: mitigating now: cordon + drain low-priority first. running: ```
kubectl cordon gpu-wn-17
kubectl drain gpu-wn-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app=batch-runner' --grace-period=60
```

ops-bot: Automation: cordon applied to gpu-wn-17 by ops-bot. Drain initiated for pods matching selector `app=batch-runner`. ETA ~45s.

maya: after drain, freed ~10GB VRAM from batch-runner containers, VRAM usage dropped from 94% -> 78% on node. ECC error rate still elevated (repeatable).

sam: good. still seeing `gpu_vram_reserved` creeping up for a particular inference workload. suspect memory leak in model server version `model-rt-1.2.9` on two pods.

devon: can we hot-restart those model pods? prefer restart over full node reboot. will coordinate with rollout window.

sam: restarted model pods gracefully: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-rt --namespace=inference --field-selector=spec.nodeName=gpu-wn-17` — one pod bounced, VRAM usage on node dropped another 6%.

ops-bot: node health update: ECC errors still above baseline (5x normal) on gpu-wn-17. Telemetry shows thermal spike 1h ago. No immediate OOMs after restarts.

maya: customer impact check: ingestion latency for Dedicated pool customers increased ~18% for 12 min starting at 19:12 UTC. No SLO breaches yet but visible tail latency. Logged to incident tracker INC-2026-453.

sam: thanks. handing off to liz for overnight watch and follow-up. tagging reminders and runbook actions below. liz you up?

liz: oncall takeover accepted. good summary — I'll keep the node cordoned and watch ECC/thermal. if ECC persists we'll drain fully and schedule node replacement.

infra-cicd: created ticket INFRA-2247 to schedule hardware triage for gpu-wn-17 (ECC + thermal). Link: https://infra.redwood.ai/INFRA-2247

devon: quick decisions from triage:
- immediate: cordon node, drained batch pods, restarted suspect model pods (mitigated VRAM pressure)
- short term: keep node cordoned until hardware triage completes
- alerts: current `gpu_vram_usage_percent > 90` fired too frequently during normal GC flaps. propose transient suppression and tuning rules

maya: propose alert changes (will submit PR to monitoring):
1) change `gpu_vram_usage_percent` alert to lookback 5m avg and trigger at > 92% for 3m, to reduce noise from short GC spikes
2) add alert for sustained ECC error rate: `sum(rate(gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m])) by (node) > 3` with 2m window -> P1 if sustained 6m
3) create a Grafana panel showing per-node VRAM percent + ECC rate side-by-side for quick triage (dashboard link placeholder)

sam: also recommend an automated mute for `gpu_vram_usage_percent` for 30m for this node while we investigate, so ops-team isn't paged repeatedly.

ops-bot: Applying temporary mute: alerts with label node=gpu-wn-17 for rule `gpu_vram_usage_percent` muted for 30m.

infra-cicd: PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/monitoring/merge_requests/1423 — includes rule change and grafana panel JSON.

maya: sample Prometheus change (in PR):
```
- alert: GPUHighVRAM
  expr: gpu_vram_usage_percent{job="nvidia"} > 90
  for: 1m
+ alert: GPUHighVRAM
+ expr: avg_over_time(gpu_vram_usage_percent{job="nvidia"}[5m]) > 92
+ for: 3m
```

sam: good. also adding runbook note: when `gpu_vram_usage_percent` fires, check `gpu_ecc_errors_total` and thermal sensors before paging hardware team. If ECC errors present escalate immediately.

devon: action items captured in incident doc INC-2026-453:
- (P0) Hardware triage INFRA-2247 assigned to @_hardware oncall (ETA 48h)
- (P1) Adjust alerts and dashboards (monitoring team) — PR #1423
- (P1) Update runbook with escalation flow for ECC vs pure VRAM OOMs
- (P2) Post-incident RCA to include why model-rt leaked VRAM on gpu-wn-17 and whether rollout policy needs change

liz: I'll follow up overnight and confirm node replacement plan if ECC doesn't quiet down. leaving node cordoned and muted. cc @support for any customer tickets.

sam: excellent work team. please add any additional logs or traces to the incident doc. marking status: mitigated but monitoring.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-453 status updated to MONITORING by sam. All paged notifications suppressed for node gpu-wn-17 for 30m.

maya: one final ask — can we add a small dashboard card to the Console for Dedicated pools showing per-node VRAM + ECC so customer-facing SREs can glance without Grafana? filing UX ticket RD-332.

devon: filed RD-332 and linked to INC-2026-453.

liz: thanks all. handing off to overnight watch. if anything spikes I'll re-open page. good job. :thumbsup:
